ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a graticule regional map, with latitude about between 45°N and 50°N, and longitudes marked around 122°E and 125°E; there is place Jia in the figure, located near about 123°E, 45°N. The figure also marks frozen-soil-related boundaries; for example, near the dashed line is marked "≈200 days," and the right-side explanation says it is an isoline of the number of days of seasonal frozen soil. At the same time, multiple lines pass near place Jia, indicating that this area is obviously affected by frozen soil. Then reason: The question stem explains that frozen soil is widespread in this area, and combined with the location shown in the figure, it can be judged that it is located in a higher-latitude area of Northeast China, mostly a plain environment with relatively flat terrain and small gradient. In plain areas, river downcutting is weak, lateral erosion and swinging are relatively obvious, and river channels easily form a curved form. Therefore, the characteristic of the river form is winding and twisting.

In plain areas, river downcutting is weak, lateral erosion and swinging are relatively obvious, and river channels easily form a curved form. Therefore, the characteristic of the river form is winding and twisting.
